title: Influence of the first coordinate
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f$ be a sign-valued Boolean function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube. Its influence at the first coordinate equals the probability, for a uniformly chosen sign vector $x$ of length $n$, that the two functions obtained by fixing the first coordinate of $f$ to $1$ and to $-1$ take different values at $x$.
hypotheses_covered: A sign-valued Boolean function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube
